findings.title: Five runner/evidence scripts shell out with no bounded timeout, bypassing the repo's own SubprocessRunner
findings.recommendation: Migrate the three highest-consequence call sites (generate_requirements_audit:78, autonomy_scorecard:82, regenerate_quality_baseline:157) to the existing Tamoz::Evals::Harness::SubprocessRunner#capture(timeout_ms:) seam, or wrap the Open3.capture3 in Timeout.timeout where the full runner is disproportionate. No new machinery.

findings.title: adr_graph.rb and adr_traceability.rb write committed artifacts that nothing verifies
findings.recommendation: Add a --check mode to both scripts following script/adr_catalog.rb:83-90, and have adr_validate.rb invoke them the way it already invokes adr_catalog.rb:108. rake adr:validate is already in ci.

findings.title: rake fixtures:refresh omits two of the six fixture generators
findings.recommendation: Add ruby "script/generate_agent_memory_repository_fixtures" at Rakefile:280. One line.

findings.title: Two generators write to stdout while their committed artifacts are hand-redirected with no recorded command
findings.recommendation: Add --out PATH (defaulting to the committed path) plus --check to both, matching adr_catalog.rb; or, if that is unwanted, document the exact redirect in each header. Do one, not both.

findings.title: The committed quality baseline is stamped as a dirty, non-HEAD tree and nothing reconciles it
findings.recommendation: Add one clause to drift_problems: fail when the committed baseline's git.dirty is true or git.commit does not match the current HEAD. The fields already exist.

findings.title: autonomy_scorecard rewrites its committed artifact on every run, including a red non-strict run
findings.recommendation: Add "strict" => strict and the git state to the document at :118-140, exactly as regenerate_quality_baseline:244 already does.

findings.title: capture_phase2_receipt embeds a per-run PID temp path in a committed evidence artifact
findings.recommendation: Use a fixed filename inside the Dir.mktmpdir block instead of Process.pid, or normalize tmpdir-prefixed argv entries in command_result:31-53.

findings.title: adr_verify.rb's fixed +/-60-character absence window can invert a true citation's expected polarity
findings.recommendation: Scope the absence decision to the sentence containing the citation rather than a fixed character radius.

findings.title: The four ADR scripts disagree on how an ADR's state is derived
findings.recommendation: Align adr_traceability.rb:27 and adr_validate.rb:41 to the two-clause test already in adr_catalog.rb:26-30, or add a corpus-wide agreement assertion to adr_validate. Prefer the one-line alignment.

blind_spots: No script/ entry point was executed; every script claim is a source trace.
gems/tamoz-evals-runner/lib/tamoz/evals/benchmark/* not read - the nine benchmark scripts delegate verdicts to engines outside this row.
EnvironmentLoader not read - which keys from the repo .env reach the real-provider child of benchmark_openclaw_run:79 is not evidenced.
test/m2_evidence_test.rb, test/graph_surface_audit_test.rb, test/dependency_review_test.rb, test/legacy_session_resume_test.rb not run (budget / subprocess-spawning).
docs/P15_RELEASE_PLAN.md not read, so R01-GATE-02's intent is unsettled.

COVERAGE.md:114 says 45 files; git ls-files script/ reports 46 (script/quality/coverage_totals.rb is tracked and nested). The 45 named entries are correct as entries; the count is one short of the tracked file count.
coordinator_flags: S01-RT-01: invariant 19's kill evidence RUNS GREEN on this checkout (sqlite_raw_oracle_test 20/1261/0F, kill test not skipped) - docs/requirements-audit.json may be stale for invariant 19.

S01-RT-02: objective 4's third supporting case (agent_session_kill_matrix_test) is in SLOW_TESTS and is never reached by release_rehearsal, which runs `rake ci`. Environment-bound and lane-bound are two separate causes; limitations.md names only the first.
S01-BEN-01 needs independent challenge across all nine unbounded call sites, not just the three recommended.
The '45 files' inventory in COVERAGE.md:114 is one short of git ls-files script/ (46).

findings.title: The launcher exports the whole .env into every Bundler/Ruby child it spawns, contradicting its own C7 comment
findings.recommendation: Run the four Bundler helper calls at :65-67 and :114 through `env -i` with the same short allowlist already written at :139-140, or stop exporting in load_env and pass values to start_one explicitly. The first reuses an existing list.

findings.title: pkill/pgrep match on the literal $TAMOZ_RUNTIME_DIR, so --stop can report success while the previous worker survives
findings.recommendation: Normalize TAMOZ_RUNTIME_DIR to an expanded absolute path once (after load_env, next to :47) and use that value in both the pkill patterns and the child argv, so the two forms cannot diverge.

blind_spots: The shell script was not executed; every claim is a source read.
Whether the worker treats an empty TAMOZ_ALMS_MCP_ENDPOINT (:161) as unset or as configured-to-nothing was not verified - gems/tamoz-agent was not read.
pgrep -f behaviour against a pattern containing an unexpanded '~' is asserted from reading, not from execution.
No test covers this script: grep -rn 'start-tamoz-comms' test/ returns nothing.
coordinator_flags: The launcher does start BOTH processes (gateway :138, worker :155) - the 'silently starts only half' failure is NOT present; the failure is a liveness check that can report RUNNING for a process dying after the 8s sleep.
docs/openclaw-chat-study-refresh/product-engineering-reviews/03-implementation-evidence.md:85 already records the downstream consequence; cite it rather than re-deriving it.

findings.title: rake ci does not run the quality gates its own documentation claims, and the one it does run no-ops without enola
findings.recommendation: Two edits at the existing owner: add 'quality:rubocop_gate' and 'quality:reek' to the ci array (Rakefile:444) and 'quality:coverage' and 'quality:baseline_drift' to ci_full (Rakefile:471); change the warn at Rakefile:371 to a raise so an absent enola fails rather than skips. Add one test that loads the Rakefile and asserts ci and ci_full's prerequisite sets. No provisioning step, no new abstraction.

findings.title: The release rehearsal runs `rake ci` while its own comment and the release plan call it the full gate
findings.recommendation: Change :157 to "ci_full", record the rake task name in the step note, and assert it in test/release_rehearsal_evidence_test.rb. If the intent is genuinely `ci`, correct the comment at :20 and plan section 10 instead - but the two must agree.

findings.title: rake quality is enola-only, so the aggregate quality command reports success without checking quality
findings.recommendation: Change Rakefile:425 to `task quality: %w[quality:rubocop quality:reek quality:architecture]`. One line, existing seam.

tests_run.command: ruby /tmp/rake_tasks_check.rb (loads Rakefile, prints Task#prerequisites, invokes nothing)

blind_spots: rake ci / ci_full / quality:* were not executed (explicitly forbidden and over budget), so the wall-clock effect of adding quality:reek to ci is not measured.
No test asserts any ci/ci_full prerequisite list - not found - so the divergence could not be caught by the suite.
coordinator_flags: R01-GATE-01 and R01-GATE-04 share a root cause; consider merging into one finding with two citations.
R01-GATE-02 needs an intent decision (fix the script to ci_full vs fix the plan to ci) before the recommendation is final.
The R01-GATE-01 challenge must MEASURE the ci wall clock after adding quality:reek against CiBudget::BUDGET_SECONDS = 60.0 (Rakefile:431), which is where this recommendation could backfire.
ci_full adds exactly [adr:verify, test, test_slow] over ci and nothing more - confirmed by enumerating the loaded task graph.
